statement: A rectangle measures 8 cm by 5 cm. A 2 cm by 2 cm square is cut out from the middle of one of the long sides, leaving a notch. What is the perimeter, in cm, of the shape that remains?

choices.misconception: I thought cutting out a square never changes the perimeter, which is only true when the square comes from a corner.
I subtracted the 2 cm gap in the long side and forgot the three new edges of the notch.
I added all four sides of the small square, 8 cm, instead of the three new edges minus the gap.
I worked out the area of the shape, 40 - 4, instead of its perimeter.

hints: Trace the edge of the new shape with your finger.
Start from the rectangle's perimeter. Ask what the cut removes from the outline and what it adds: the notch removes part of one side but creates new edges inside the shape.
The rectangle has perimeter 26. The cut removes 2 cm of the long side and adds three edges of 2 cm.

solutions.reliable: The rectangle's perimeter is 2 x (8 + 5) = 26 cm. Cutting the notch removes 2 cm of the long side but adds the notch's two side walls and its floor, 3 x 2 = 6 cm. The new perimeter is 26 - 2 + 6 = 30 cm. The transferable idea: when a shape is cut, track what leaves the outline and what joins it, instead of assuming the perimeter shrinks with the area.
solutions.elegant: Push the notch's floor back out to the long side and it exactly fills the gap, so only the two 2 cm walls are extra: 26 + 4 = 30.

whyOnTest: Perimeter and area move in opposite directions here, and the corner-cut fact students remember gives the wrong answer for a notch.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
